newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coles slide from record high accelerates.
newsitem.headline: Coles slide from record high accelerates.

text.p: The slide of shares in Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer Ltd from its recent record high accelerated on Monday as traders took the broader market weakness as an excuse to further lighten positions.

Coles shares have tumbled from the all-time peak of A$7.12 on July 4 to A$6.53 by 2.55 p.m. (0455 GMT) today, with market players citing overvaluations relative to the retail sector and the death of a short covering rally after the conversion of preference shares on June 5.
"It had run ahead of itself. At A$7.00 it was comparatively overpriced," said Daiwa Securities analyst, Rosalie James, noting its valuation relative to main rival Woolworths.
Others concurred, noting that the buying interest had dried up within recent days after some big traders had covered their positions.

"Some of the institutions were apparently short after the preference issue and that drove some of the interest at least," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage, pointing to a very thin buy side in the retailer's stocks.
"There is not much there at all, but if you look at the sell side there are some good size parcels."
The exit of traders from Coles failed to help Woolworths shares which were seven cents lower at A$4.13 in the soft overall market by 3.20 p.m. (0520 GMT).
At the same time, Coles shares were trading 26 cents lower at A$6.54 on turnover of 819,755 shares.
